source.authors: Jonathan H. Cohen, Jørgen Berge, Mark A. Moline, Asgeir J. Sørensen, Kim Last, Stig Falk-Petersen, Paul E. Renaud, Eva S. Leu, Julie Grenvald, Finlo Cottier, Heather Cronin, Sebastian Menze, Petter Norgren, Øystein Varpe, Malin Daase, Gerald Darnis, Geir Johnsen
source.title: Is Ambient Light during the High Arctic Polar Night Sufficient to Act as a Visual Cue for Zooplankton?

method: electroretinogram (subcorneal tungsten microelectrode), spectral sensitivity by the criterion response method, 5 individuals; peak given as a region of the curve
conditions: Wild-caught Arctic krill: zooplankton collected from Kongsfjorden (Svalbard) with a 180 um WP2 net lowered vertically from a small boat down to 75 m; Thysanoessa inermis, body length 12.3 +/- 1.43 mm (standard error, n = 5). Eye stalk and dorsal carapace glued to an acrylic support, animal submerged in a temperature-controlled water bath at 4.5 C (+/- 0.6 SD, n = 5), epoxy-insulated tungsten microelectrode positioned subcorneally; preparations survived 6 to 22 h of recording. Spectral sensitivity was measured in 5 individuals by the criterion response method (details deferred to cited earlier papers). The paper does not state a dark-adaptation period in the Methods paragraph, the stimulus source, intensity steps or the wavelengths tested, and does not state that stimuli were equal-quantum; the Results give a curve peak range only, not a single wavelength or per-animal peaks. The fitted pigment (lambda max 492 nm, specific absorbance 0.010 per um, residual sum of squares 0.0267, photoreceptor length 56 um) is a template model of the ERG curve, not a microspectrophotometric measurement (separate record). Aim of the paper is whether polar-night skylight is detectable (modelled detection to roughly 20-30 m); the ERG is the only physiology reported.
quote: Electroretinogram recording from T. inermis eyes yielded a visual spectral sensitivity curve that peaked in the 470–490 nm region (Fig 2).
note: Whole Results sentence (21 words) read verbatim in two abutting pieces in one response ('...sensitivity curve' | 'that peaked in the 470-490 nm region (Fig 2).') and joined identically on a second pass; the en dash read as printed. new trait for this species: erg_peak_nm, a whole-eye ERG sensitivity maximum as used on main (e.g. Anomalops katoptron), distinct from the template-fitted pigment value (lambda_max_nm record). Value is the authors' range, not a single wavelength. Family and order as filed on main for other Euphausiidae (Euphausiacea); the name appears as Thysanoessa inermis (Krøyer, 1846) on a GBIF species page returned by search, with Thysanopoda inermis and Boreophausia inermis listed separately as synonyms; not in gbif-names.tsv; WoRMS/OBIS not opened (refused/failed). Not on main under this DOI or species (grep of docs/ for Thysanoessa and the DOI: progress note desk-d176 records the page as rate-limited then). Licence: page states the article is free of all copyright (public-domain wording) and Crossref lists CC0 1.0 (publicdomain/zero), content-version vor. Crossref authors, volume 10, issue 6 and issued 2015 agree with the page byline. A companion study (PLoS Biol 3001413, same species, wild-caught, ERG V-logI sensitivity changes with time of day) reports no numeric Log K in text and was not filed.

method: template (rhodopsin) fit to the ERG spectral sensitivity data of 5 individuals; model-derived absorbance maximum, not microspectrophotometry
conditions: Wild-caught Arctic krill: zooplankton collected from Kongsfjorden (Svalbard) with a 180 um WP2 net lowered vertically from a small boat down to 75 m; Thysanoessa inermis, body length 12.3 +/- 1.43 mm (standard error, n = 5). quote: These data were best-fit by a rhodopsin visual pigment with maximum absorbance (λmax) of 492 nm …
note: Sentence cut after the value; cut text (read verbatim in a separate pass) is ', and a specific absorbance of 0.010 um-1 (residual sum of squares = 0.0267)' and the cut drops no qualifier of the 492 nm. The fit comes from the criterion-response ERG curve of 5 individuals (same sentence block as the erg_peak_nm record), using a visual pigment template cited as ref. 33 and a photoreceptor length of 56 um from semi-thin sections of animals from the same collections; value is a modelled best-fit, not an isolated-pigment measurement, and the paper gives no fit statistic for the lambda max itself beyond the residual sum of squares. Family/order, name, licence and Crossref check as for the erg_peak_nm record. Not on main for this species.

value: mainly attacked the 5 mm bead (of 5 mm and 12 mm black beads)

source.authors: Tammy M. Duong, Ann B. Gomez, Thomas N. Sherratt
source.title: Response of adult dragonflies to artificial prey of different size and colour

method: field prey-choice test: single black bead prey (5 mm or 12 mm) offered on a pole to wild free-flying dragonflies; attack within 120 s ; this line: Leucorrhinia intacta (the smaller species)
conditions: Field experiment with free-flying wild adults of two co-occurring species at the East Field meadow near Queen's University Biological Station, Ontario, 3 to 17 July 2015, 0900 to 1500 h. A single black bead of 5 mm or 12 mm diameter was hung 100 cm below a 183 cm bamboo pole and offered to a dragonfly located in the field for at most 120 s; time to attack analysed with a Cox proportional hazards model (R survival package) with species, sex, bead size and their two-way interactions. Totals: 49 attacks from 131 presentations by the two species together; per-species and per-bead-size counts are not in the text (Table 2 not read). Tested individuals were not marked, so repeat testing of the same individual cannot be excluded. Nulls and limits: the species x prey-size interaction was not significant (z = 1.539, P = 0.1238), so the contrast between a species that took both sizes and one that mainly took 5 mm rests on the main species effect and the stated pattern, not on an interaction test; in the separate community experiment (13 species pooled, 1,153 presentations) prey colour pattern had no effect on attack decisions (z = 0.585, P = 0.559) and there was no colour x size interaction (z = -0.785, P = 0.433), and the prey size x dragonfly size interaction was significant (chi2 = 6.039, P = 0.0134) there; those pooled results are not species values. The measured response is the attack decision to an artificial prey bead of one of two sizes, not an acuity or detection threshold; the paper reports no contrast or luminance matching of beads to the background in the text read. Sexes were recorded and females attacked more often (z = 2.355, P = 0.0185) in the community experiment.
quote: The probability of prey being attacked was higher overall when prey were presented to L. pulchella than L. intacta (z = -2.947, P = 0.0032), as L. pulchella attacked both prey sizes while L. intacta mainly attacked 5 mm prey…
note: Whole Results sentence of 42 words, cut after 'prey' (trailing figure reference '(Fig 4).' dropped, marked by the ellipsis) to meet the 40-word limit; read verbatim in four abutting pieces in one response and re-read on a second pass with a different split giving the same join. One sentence supports both species lines and each value is confined to its own clause (audit 334). Leucorrhinia intacta is the clause 'L. intacta mainly attacked 5 mm prey'; the quote does not give the proportion or counts. Libellulidae, Odonata as in main's insect-view cells for this species; not in gbif-names.tsv (no SYNONYM row). Not on main under this DOI or species+behaviour_vision (the species appear on main only as acuity/cff/interommatidial gap cells; desk-d232 held this paper because key sentences were over the tool limit and it did not read them whole). Crossref authors (Duong, Gomez, Sherratt), volume 12, issue 6 and issued 2017 agree with the page.

value: attacked both bead sizes (5 mm and 12 mm black beads); overall attack probability higher than L. intacta (z = -2.947, P = 0.0032)
